items.stem: What does Snowflake's separation of storage and compute allow?

options.text: Scaling compute (warehouses) independently of stored data
options.rationale: Correct: compute can scale up or down without changing storage.

options.text: Deleting data whenever a warehouse is resized
options.rationale: Resizing compute does not touch stored data.

options.text: Running queries with no compute at all
options.rationale: Queries still require a running warehouse.

options.text: Storing data only inside the warehouse
options.rationale: Storage is separate from the compute warehouses.

items.explanation: Correct: compute can scale up or down without changing storage.

items.stem: Which TWO habits help an analyst control Snowflake compute cost? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Enable auto-suspend so idle warehouses stop consuming credits
options.rationale: Correct: auto-suspend stops paying for idle compute.

options.text: Use an appropriately sized warehouse for the workload
options.rationale: Correct: right-sizing avoids paying for unused capacity.

options.text: Leave a large warehouse running continuously just in case
Re-run identical queries to avoid the result cache
options.rationale: Avoiding the cache wastes compute unnecessarily.

items.explanation: Correct: auto-suspend stops paying for idle compute.

items.stem: Two accounts need access to the same live dataset without duplicating it. What fits best?

options.rationale: Correct: secure sharing gives live access without copying data.

options.text: Exporting and emailing CSV files daily
options.rationale: That duplicates data and goes stale immediately.

options.text: Copying the whole database to each account
options.rationale: Copying duplicates storage and causes drift.
That violates least privilege and does not address sharing.

items.explanation: Correct: secure sharing gives live access without copying data.
